decisions.decision: The cost hard cap is enforced INSIDE SupervisedInvocationRunner.Run, not in a wrapper and not in Orchestrator.BeforeProvider. SupervisedInvocationRunner gains a required field Ledger *CostLedger and a required field Preflight ProviderPreflight; a zero-value or partially-built SupervisedInvocationRunner returns an error and starts no process. The order inside Run is strictly: (1) refuse if Ledger, Preflight, Supervisor or Log is nil; (2) Ledger.Reserve(...) which reads and rewrites the ledger file and fsyncs it; (3) resolve argv[0] and exec through ProcessSupervisor; (4) Ledger.TrueUp(...) from the parsed total_cost_usd. No other order is acceptable and no path may skip step 2.
decisions.rationale: A decorator (BudgetedInvocationRunner wrapping SupervisedInvocationRunner) can be bypassed by any caller who constructs the inner type directly, and Orchestrator.BeforeProvider is too far from the syscall - it runs once per Execution, not once per invocation, and it is an optional hook (nil is legal today). Making the ledger a required dependency of the only type that owns a ProcessSupervisor in the provider path means there is no constructible object that can spawn the CLI without first debiting the ledger. This is the same discipline dp-v2-012 d5 applied to Google Cloud: the guard is a precondition of the object, not a step in a procedure someone may forget.

decisions.decision: Reserve worst case before the process starts, true up from the real figure afterwards, and never let true-up increase the count. Formula, evaluated under an exclusive lock on the ledger file: refuse unless outstanding_count + 1 <= limits.max_invocations AND settled_total_usd + reserved_total_usd + limits.worst_case_reservation_usd <= limits.max_total_cost_usd. worst_case_reservation_usd is 1.00 and max_total_cost_usd is 10.00, both read from the approved preflight record, never from Go constants. On success the ledger gains an entry {sequence, purpose, state:"reserved", reserved_usd:1.00, started_at}; the file is written to a temp file in the same directory, fsynced, and renamed over the old one BEFORE exec. After Adapter.Parse succeeds the same entry becomes {state:"settled", actual_usd:<total_cost_usd>, session_id, finished_at} and is written the same way. TrueUp only ever lowers the accounted amount and never removes the entry.
decisions.rationale: Structurally identical to internal/quota's Reserve/TrueUp pair (quota.go: Reserve admits against a pre-checked worst case, TrueUp credits down and never grows), so there is one accounting pattern in this repository rather than two. Persisting the reservation before exec is what makes a crash fail closed: a runner killed mid-invocation leaves a reserved entry that keeps charging the worst case, so the ceiling can only ever be over-estimated, never under. The 1.00 worst case is roughly ten times the measured floor (0.077 and 0.105 USD for a minimal probe, because the CLI's own system prompt cache creation is billed on every invocation), which leaves headroom for a genuinely long invocation without letting a single run consume the whole budget.

decisions.decision: Fail closed, spawning nothing, in every one of these cases: the ledger file cannot be read; it parses but does not match the ledger schema; its provider or task_id does not match the current run; its halted flag is true; the approved provider preflight record for this task_id is missing, is not schema-valid, or fails CheckProviderPreflightLedger's record-level rules; the record's limits disagree with the ledger file's recorded limits; the resolved executable path does not exist or is not the path the record declares; the formula in d2 is not satisfied. Additionally, if any settled actual_usd exceeds 2.00, set halted:true in the ledger, return a distinct terminal error, and stop the whole run: every later Reserve then fails closed regardless of remaining budget.
decisions.rationale: Sol's rule is that an unreadable ledger must not spawn. Enumerating the refusal set exhaustively is what turns that from an intention into a test matrix - each item is one negative test. The persistent halted flag matters because a single 2.00+ invocation means the cost model is wrong, and a wrong cost model plus remaining budget is exactly how a bounded experiment becomes an unbounded one; halting in the file rather than in memory means a restarted runner cannot forget.

decisions.decision: The ledger file lives outside the repository and outside every workspace, at the absolute path declared by the approved record's limits.ledger_path, which for this task is /home/takushi/.local/state/agentic-loop/v2/V2-017-provider-cost.json, created 0600 in a 0700 directory. Its shape is {schema_version, provider, task_id, preflight_digest, limits{max_invocations,max_total_cost_usd,worst_case_reservation_usd}, halted, entries[]}. preflight_digest is the sha256 of the approved record file and is re-verified on every Reserve.
decisions.rationale: Outside the repository so a billed fact can never be lost by a git operation or silently rewritten by a task's own commit, and outside the workspace so the child process the ledger is metering cannot reach it - the same reasoning BoundedLog already applies to the diagnostic log. Re-verifying preflight_digest on every Reserve means editing the approved ceiling after the fact invalidates the ledger instead of raising the cap.

decisions.decision: SupervisedInvocationRunner does not hand the real CLI's stdout to Adapter.Parse. It projects it, in memory, into the minimal fixture shape the adapter accepts and hands only the projection onward. Success projects to {"type":"result","subtype":"success","checkpoint":"claude:<session_id>","output":"sha256:<hex of the CLI's result string>","usage":{"input_tokens":N,"output_tokens":M,"total_tokens":N+M}}. Failure projects to {"type":"result","subtype":"error","status":"error","code":"<code>","error":"<already-safe short message>","exit_code":<n>}. The raw stdout buffer is never written to any file, is capped at provider.MaxFixtureBytes, and is dropped as soon as the projection is built.
decisions.rationale: Two hard constraints force this. First, provider.parseFixture uses decoder.DisallowUnknownFields() against a fixture struct that has no total_cost_usd, session_id, duration_api_ms, duration_ms, is_error, uuid, num_turns, permission_denials or modelUsage field, so the real CLI's JSON is rejected outright as ErrInvalidFixture - and internal/provider/** is a prohibited path, so the struct cannot be widened. Second, V2-016's crash-resume case B journals the payload bytes and re-Parses them on resume, so whatever is handed to Parse is written to disk; handing over raw CLI stdout would persist raw provider output and violate release-contract.md section 7. Projecting output to a sha256 of the model's text preserves everything the Increment Artifact digest needs (OutputDigest stays a deterministic function of the real output, so case B's digest comparison still works) while making it impossible for model text - or a secret-shaped string inside it, which provider.secret.Match would otherwise reject - to reach the journal. The runner's doc comment already scopes it exactly this way: it produces fixture bytes for Adapter.Parse and never itself decides success or failure.

decisions.decision: argv[0] resolution: ClaudeAdapter.Build emits the bare name "claude" and ProcessSupervisor uses exec.Command, which resolves through PATH - and devbox run --pure strips PATH, so the bare name is not resolvable in the validated environment. SupervisedInvocationRunner therefore replaces argv[0] with the approved record's provider.executable_path, but only after asserting filepath.Base(executable_path) == argv[0]; otherwise it refuses. The argv actually executed (absolute path plus the adapter's flags) is what gets recorded in evidence.
decisions.rationale: Keeping the substitution inside the runner leaves internal/provider untouched (prohibited path) and keeps the adapter provider-neutral. Asserting the basename match is what stops the substitution from becoming an arbitrary-executable hole: the record can point the runner at a different copy of claude, never at a different program. Recording the resolved argv rather than the adapter's argv is what G3 needs, because the resolved form is the only one that proves which binary on this machine actually ran.

decisions.decision: ProcessSupervisor gains two additive fields, Stdin []byte and Stdout io.Writer, defaulting to today's behaviour when zero. It currently plumbs neither, so the Work Packet on stdin and the JSON on stdout have nowhere to go. Do not change Run's signature and do not change the process-group TERM-then-KILL logic; TestSupervisorCancelsProcessGroupTERMThenKILL must keep passing unmodified.
decisions.rationale: Additive fields keep every existing caller and the strengthened V2-016 supervisor test working, which matters because that test was proven non-vacuous by a before/after experiment recorded in ev-v2-016-runner. A new method would duplicate the kill logic, which is the one part of this file nobody should have two copies of.

decisions.decision: Credential isolation for claude is proven as an absence, because the Secret Broker has nothing to hand over: the claude CLI reads its own store at ~/.claude/.credentials.json (verified present, mode 0600) and takes no credential from argv or environment. Concretely: (a) the approved record declares environment.granted_names as the empty array, which contracts validateProviderPreflight enforces for provider.name == "claude" (dp-v2-047 d8 rule 4); (b) the SecretBroker allowlist for provider "claude" is empty, so SecretBroker.Lease for any name returns ErrSecretNotAllowed - asserted as a positive control, so the emptiness is measured rather than declared; (c) no Grant is attached to the ProviderClient for the live run, and the built Invocation.Environment is asserted set-equal to the record's environment.base_names, which is the minimum the CLI needs (HOME so it can find its own store, PATH, and whatever else invocation 2 proves to be necessary, each entry justified in the evidence); (d) GuardEnvironment against exactly that allowlist and GuardCommand over the resolved argv both pass; (e) the six-target absence scan of V2-016's A11 test is re-run against the live invocation - journal file, marshalled Work Packet, bounded log file, canonical store EventsPage events, marshalled AcceptResultResponse, and every element of os.Args and Invocation.Argv - asserting no match of the runner's secretValue pattern and no occurrence of any value present in the child environment; (f) an AST scan asserts no non-test file under internal/runner references ".claude", ".credentials" or any path under the user's home, so the Control Plane and the runner never open the credential store at all. The mechanism's own liveness stays proven by V2-016's existing canary test, which leases a crypto/rand fixture for a synthetic provider and asserts it appears in Invocation.Environment and nowhere else.
decisions.rationale: The honest claim here is not "the credential was handled safely" but "the credential never entered our address space". That is a stronger property and it needs a different proof shape: absence plus a positive control that the absence is not vacuous. (b) and (f) are what make it non-vacuous - without (b), an empty allowlist and a broken allowlist look identical; without (f), 'we did not log it' and 'we never read it' look identical. Never read ~/.claude/.credentials.json in a test, not even to build a canary predicate: a test that reads a real credential in order to prove the credential is not leaked has leaked it into the test process.

decisions.decision: Eight nominal invocations, each mapped one-to-one to a proof, ceiling 16 leaving eight retry slots. I1 happy: the full journey from requirement intake to Increment Artifact with the real CLI (proves M3 condition 1 and, with I2, condition 3); its journaled projection is also the input to crash-resume case B, which consumes no further invocation. I2 happy: wire and identity capture - the resolved absolute argv runs, the real JSON is projected and Parsed, and session_id, usage, total_cost_usd, duration_api_ms, duration_ms and num_turns are captured into the ledger and the evidence (proves the run was a real CLI, G3). I3 happy: the credential-isolation observation run of d8 (a)-(f) against a real invocation (proves M3 condition 4). I4 happy: a second Increment on the same Repository across more than one LeaseTTL of LeaseKeeper ticks, proving lease renewal and checkpoint continuity hold with a real process in the middle (proves the M3 deliverable '1 Repository/1 Incrementの変更、検証、integration' under a real Provider). I5 crash: SIGKILL of the process group mid-invocation before any result is journaled (proves the supervisor's group kill reaches a real CLI's children; its ledger entry stays reserved at worst case forever, which is the intended fail-closed accounting for an unknown charge). I6 crash: the resumed Execution re-runs the provider exactly once under a new ExecutionID with a strictly greater fencing token, and the crashed attempt's late AcceptResult is rejected with domain.ErrLeaseExpired (proves M3 condition 2, case A). I7 error: a real CLI error path, induced deterministically and without an API call by pointing the CLI at an unreachable base URL, asserting the failure is classified and the Execution ends failed with no retry to green. I8 cancel: context cancellation during a real invocation, asserting TERM-then-KILL of the group, FailureCancelled, no journaled result, and the reservation retained at worst case. Crash-resume needs I5 and I6 only because case B reuses I1's journal.
decisions.rationale: A one-to-one map is what makes the budget auditable: any invocation that cannot name the sentence it proves is an invocation nobody authorised. I7 costs approximately nothing because the request never reaches the API, yet it is still a real error from the real binary rather than a fixture, which is the distinction that matters; inducing it by environment rather than by argv keeps internal/provider untouched. Note that I7 exercises transport failure, not model failure, and must be described that way - the per-Provider success/error/quota/cancel matrix is M6's condition and this task proves only the representative Provider's half of it. The eight spare slots exist for re-measurement after a code fix, not for re-rolling a red result. Worst-case arithmetic: sixteen unsettled reservations would be 16.00 USD, above the 10.00 ceiling, so the dollar ceiling binds first at ten unsettled runs; once settled at the measured 0.08-0.11 USD each, the sixteen-invocation count ceiling is what binds. Both are correct fail-closed behaviour and the interaction must be stated in the evidence rather than discovered at run time.

decisions.decision: Reaching either ceiling is a capacity-exhaustion stop, not a result. On exhaustion or on the 2.00 anomaly halt: stop immediately, do not start another invocation, do not register an evidence record claiming passed, and escalate with the ledger snapshot (entries, settled total, outstanding reservations) and the list of invocations whose proof was not obtained. If an evidence record is registered at all in that state, its result must be partial, the unobtained checks must carry status skipped, and each summary must say which proof is missing and why.
decisions.rationale: release-contract.md section 9's discipline is that retrying until green is not evidence. The failure mode this guards against is the tempting one: eight of the nine proofs land, the budget runs out, and the record quietly omits the ninth. A partial record that names the gap is worth more than a passed record that hides it, and it is the only form that lets a human decide whether to raise the ceiling.

decisions.decision: Live tests never run by default and never run inside make check. Each live test skips unless all three hold: the environment variable AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_PROVIDER=1 is set, the approved record exists at .agents/v2/provider-preflight/V2-017-provider-live-claude.json and passes contracts validation, and the ledger path from that record is writable. Because devbox run --pure strips the environment, the live suite is invoked as: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_PROVIDER=1 -e HOME=/home/takushi -e PATH=/home/takushi/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin -- go test -count=1 -v -run TestProviderLive ./internal/runner. A test asserting that make check starts no process is part of the acceptance.
decisions.rationale: A cost-bearing test that runs by default would bill CI and would bill every future contributor's make check. Gating on the approved record as well as on the environment variable means the gate and the approval are the same gate, so there is no way to run live without an approval in the tree. The explicit -e list is required because AGENTIC_LOOP_TEST_GROUP-style variables are silently dropped by devbox run --pure; a test that skips because its gate variable vanished would look green while proving nothing, which is why the skip must be logged with t.Logf naming which of the three conditions failed.

decisions.decision: Evidence records the CLI's identity in checks[] and artifact_refs, because contracts/schemas/evidence.json has additionalProperties:false and no field for provider telemetry. One checks[] entry per invocation, with argv set to the resolved absolute argv that really ran, working_directory set to the absolute workspace path, and summary carrying: provider name, CLI version 2.1.241, the executable's absolute path and the symlink it resolved to, session_id, usage as in/out/cache-read/cache-creation counts, total_cost_usd, duration_api_ms, duration_ms, num_turns, the classification of the outcome, and the OutputDigest. artifact_refs carries one entry {artifact_id:"provider-preflight", media_type:"application/json", sha256:<digest of the approved record>, size_bytes, name}. Never record the prompt, the Work Packet contents, or any part of the model's response text; the projection's sha256 is the only representation of the output that is allowed to appear.
decisions.rationale: This is the only place the evidence schema leaves room, and it is enough: summary is an unbounded string and argv is exactly the machine-readable field the 'real process was started' claim needs. Deliberately avoid writing the substring 'token' anywhere in these summaries (write usage as in/out/cache-read/cache-creation counts, not as *_tokens) because gitleaks' generic-api-key rule is keyword-triggered and 'token' on a line invites it to capture the neighbouring quoted value; this costs nothing and avoids needing a new .gitleaks.toml allowlist. The artifact_refs digest is what CheckProviderPreflightLedger uses to bind this evidence to its approval.

decisions.decision: Record session_id verbatim in evidence and as the checkpoint prefixed with "claude:". Flag the interpretation to product_orchestrator rather than deciding it unilaterally.
decisions.rationale: release-contract.md section 7 enumerates what evidence may retain as 'Provider、version、capability、時刻、結果、消費量' and a provider-issued session identifier is not literally in that list, though it is plainly part of 結果 in the sense that matters - it is the provider's own handle for the run, and it is what makes the claim 'this run really happened at the provider' checkable rather than asserted. It is also required as the checkpoint: digesting it would leave a resumption handle that cannot resume. The tension is real and belongs to whoever owns the invariant, so it is recorded here and escalated, with the fallback being to keep the verbatim value only in the out-of-repository ledger and put sha256(session_id) in the evidence.

decisions.decision: The approved record .agents/v2/provider-preflight/V2-017-provider-live-claude.json is written by this task, but its approval block - approver, approved_at, approval_reference - is supplied by the human owner, and approval.subject_path/subject_digest bind it to sha256 of .agents/v2/packets/V2-017-work-order.json. Do not author, guess or backdate an approval. If the Work Order is edited after approval the digest no longer matches and the ledger check fails: that is intended, and the response is re-approval, not editing the digest.
decisions.rationale: A self-approved cost ceiling is not a ceiling. Binding the approval to the Work Order's bytes is what makes 'approved for this scope' mean something a machine can check, and accepting that a Work Order edit invalidates it is the price of that meaning.

verification: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_PROVIDER=1 -e HOME=/home/takushi -e PATH=/home/takushi/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin -- go test -count=1 -v -run 'TestProviderLive' ./internal/runner
risks: A model response containing a secret-shaped string would be rejected by provider.parseFixture's secret.Match if the raw text ever reached Parse. The d5 projection removes the exposure entirely by sending only a sha256; if the projection is ever changed to carry text, this risk returns.

Killing the CLI mid-invocation (I5, I8) may still have been billed for tokens already consumed, and the true amount is unknowable from outside. The ledger deliberately keeps the worst case reserved forever for those entries, which over-states spend. If that over-statement exhausts the budget before the eight proofs land, that is a capacity-exhaustion stop under d10, not a reason to release the reservation.

The CLI's minimum environment is not known in advance; only HOME and PATH are confidently required. Discovering it empirically costs invocations. Mitigation: discover it during I2 and record the final base_names list with a justification per entry. If more than four variables turn out to be needed, stop and escalate rather than widening the allowlist quietly.

The ledger's absolute path is machine-specific and is committed inside the approved record, which makes the record non-portable. Accepted for M3 local; a portable form belongs to whoever generalises this beyond one machine.

The 2.00 anomaly halt is a one-way door written into a file outside the repository. If it trips spuriously the task stops until a human clears it. That is the intended asymmetry, but it must be documented in the runbook or the next operator will not know where to look.
gitleaks git scans every ref in the shared repository, so make secrets can be red for another branch's bytes. Diagnose by the reported File before touching .gitleaks.toml.

This task cannot start until V2-047 has merged: the provider-preflight schema, validateProviderPreflight and CheckProviderPreflightLedger are all V2-047 deliverables and all three are prohibited paths here.
